title: Programmer productivity and performance on AMD's AI Engines: Offloading Fortran intrinsics via MLIR a case-study
problem: Specialized architectures (FPGAs, AI Engines) offer energy efficiency but require substantial expertise to program; programmers prefer familiar languages like Fortran
method: MLIR-based Fortran intrinsic offloading to AMD AIE; lower MLIR linear algebra dialect to AIE dialects; demonstrate for Fortran intrinsics on Ryzen AI CPU; no code modifications required

title: Megabits Down to Kilobits: Memory-Efficient Time-Aware Shaping for TSN
problem: Memory-efficient Time-Aware Shaper (TAS) for Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN) in cyber-physical systems; traditional TAS stores per-frame gate control rules requiring tens of megabits of memory, exceeding switch capacity.
method: METAS (Memory-Efficient TAS) transitions from per-frame to per-flow rule storage: stores one persistent rule per flow and dynamically generates temporary frame rules on-demand. FPGA prototype demonstrates memory reduction from 14.34 Mbits to 288 Kbits for 1,024 flows using only 1.56% of FPGA logic resources while maintaining microsecond-level latency and nanosecond-level jitter.

title: Approximate SMT Counting Beyond Discrete Domains
problem: Satisfiability Modulo Theory (SMT) solvers handle complex hybrid formulas with discrete and continuous variables, but extending them to model counting—especially for discrete projections in hybrid formulas—is challenging; existing methods like bit-blasting cannot handle continuous variables.
method: pact is an SMT model counter using hashing-based approximate model counting with theoretical error guarantees. It makes logarithmic SMT solver calls relative to projection variables, using optimized hash functions to partition solution spaces and approximate discrete projections in hybrid formulas.

title: 6.7 A 10b Source-Driver IC with All-Channel Automatic Offset Calibration and Slew-Rate-Enhanced Amplifier Achieving 2273pm2/Channel and 1.9mV DVO for 6285-PPI OLED-on-Silicon Displays
problem: Microdisplays for AR/VR (4K×4K, >120Hz refresh) require compact, high-pixel-density source-driver ICs; OLED-on-Silicon (OLEDoS) integrates pixel/driving circuits on silicon but demands tight area budgets (2273pm²/ch) and low display voltage offset (DVO) for color fidelity.
method: 10-bit source-driver IC with all-channel automatic offset calibration and slew-rate-enhanced amplifier on OLEDoS backplane; achieves 2273pm²/channel area and 1.9mV DVO for 6285 PPI display through integrated low-area calibration and fast-slew output stage.

title: Will We Ever have Truly Secure Operating Systems?
problem: Operating system kernels remain a dominant attack surface despite decades of security research; formal proofs of OS security have historically been limited to small microkernels and have not scaled to binary-level or general-purpose OS kernels.
method: The paper surveys the seL4 microkernel verification program, which produced a proof chain from C implementation correctness, down to binary-level verification, through to security enforcement proofs (confidentiality, integrity) and sound worst-case execution-time analysis, covering 4 ISAs. The approach uses interactive theorem provers (Isabelle/HOL) to formally connect abstract security policies to compiled binary behavior, then discusses speculative early-stage work on extending this methodology to a provably secure general-purpose OS.

title: 1.2 From Chips to Thoughts: Building Physical Intelligence into Robotic Systems
problem: Generative AI deployment in robotics and edge systems faces high energy costs for both training and inference on large multi-modal models, constraining real-time autonomous system deployment.
method: Physical intelligence architecture for robotic systems integrating energy-efficient AI computation, sensorimotor feedback, and real-time control through optimized chip design and system-level power management.

title: InferCT: An Efficient and Generalizable Framework to Enable 3D Machine Learning for Computed Tomography
problem: 3D deep learning models for CT inference require large GPU memory, limiting practical deployment. Existing approaches struggle with dataset size variability and imaging task diversity.
method: InferCT partitions CT volumes into cubic sub-volumes fitting GPU memory, distributing across multiple GPUs. Adds vendor-agnostic optimizations: lock-free shared memory data structure, pipeline execution to hide prefetching/post-processing latency, and parallel data loader.

title: 14.7 NeuroPilot: A 28nm, 69.4fJ/node and 0.22ns/node, 32×32 Mimetic-Path-Searching CIM-Macro with Dynamic-Logic Pilot PE and Dual-Direction Searching
problem: Path-finding algorithms for autonomous micro-robots, VLSI routing, and wavefront propagation traditionally use digital accelerators; existing mimetic-CIM solutions suffer from inefficient single-direction searching (underutilization), poor DFF-based storage (power/area/leakage), and limited processing windows for large maps.
method: NeuroPilot implements dual-direction searching (DDS) to accelerate by utilizing full search time, uses a dynamic-logic pilot PE with outspread pre-charge (OPC) circuit for superior PPA and reduced leakage vs. DFF storage, and enables 3-step coarse/fine-path (TsCFP) flow for efficient large-map navigation.

title: Selectively Uniform Concurrency Testing
problem: Randomized concurrency testing algorithms fail to uniformly sample thread interleavings, causing them to miss bugs that manifest only in rare, infrequent interleavings. Prior algorithms are biased in their sampling, leading to poor coverage of the exponentially large interleaving space.
method: SURW (Selectively Uniform Random Walk) is an online randomized concurrency testing algorithm that achieves interleaving-uniformity by carefully selecting a subset of program events and applying a uniform sampling strategy over their interleaving space. The algorithm operates as a black-box randomized technique that requires only minimal additional information about the program to achieve uniformity over broad classes of programs and arbitrary event subsets.

title: Wave: Offloading Resource Management to SmartNIC Cores
problem: Userspace system software tasks (kernel thread scheduling, memory management, RPC stacks) consume scarce host CPU cores in cloud servers, reducing the compute available to paying tenants. Existing SmartNIC offload frameworks require custom APIs and cannot handle microsecond-scale system software latencies without host CPU involvement.
method: Wave is a framework that runs existing Linux userspace system software (unchanged or minimally modified) as processes/agents on mid-tier SmartNIC ARM cores. It introduces a new host-SmartNIC communication API designed to support microsecond-scale decision latencies, enabling offload of preemption-sensitive tasks such as the kernel thread scheduler. The framework uses Linux userspace system interfaces to align host OS functionality with SmartNIC capabilities, and avoids requiring custom kernel modifications on the host side.

title: Folded Banks: 3D-Stacked HBM Design for Fine-Grained Random-Access Bandwidth
problem: HBM has seen substantial improvements in sequential (peak) bandwidth across generations but irregular/random-access bandwidth has stagnated, limiting performance for applications with non-sequential memory access patterns such as graph analytics, recommendation, and sparse workloads.
method: Folded Banks (FB-HBM) redistributes DRAM bank subarrays by folding them across multiple dies in a 3D stack and relocating command/control logic and global sense amplifiers to a new dedicated base layer implemented in a logic process. Intra-bank column select lines (CSLs) and master data lines (MDLs) are routed vertically through thin-pitch through-silicon vias (TSVs) and hybrid bonds, dramatically reducing RC power losses from long horizontal routing. Self-timed sense amplifiers eliminate the need for costly dummy subarrays, further reducing power and area on the DRAM dies.

title: 37.5 SKADI: A 28nm Complete K-SAT Solver Featuring Dual-Path SRAM-Based Macro and Incremental Update with 100% Solvability
problem: K-SAT (Boolean satisfiability) solvers must handle both satisfiable (SAT) and unsatisfiable (UNSAT) cases with complete proofs; prior ASIC solvers are incomplete (SAT-only), while analog approaches suffer accuracy loss and digital methods face poor area/energy efficiency.
method: 28nm ASIC K-SAT solver using dual-path SRAM-based macro for bidirectional deduction (clauses→assignments and assignments→clauses), incremental state management via efficient assignment tracking, and multi-level clause state representation for 100% correctness, avoiding analog accuracy loss.

title: Spindle: Efficient Distributed Training of Multi-Task Large Models via Wavefront Scheduling
problem: Training multi-task, multi-modal (MT MM) foundation models is inefficient because their heterogeneous model components and diverse workloads across tasks and modalities create complex dependency patterns that existing parallelism strategies cannot jointly optimize. No existing distributed training system addresses the combined challenges of workload heterogeneity and dependency-driven execution scheduling for MT MM models.
method: Spindle decomposes MT MM model execution into 'waves'—groups of heterogeneous micro-tasks—and applies a two-phase joint optimization: (1) heterogeneity-aware workload parallelization that assigns tasks to devices accounting for differing compute demands per modality, and (2) dependency-driven wavefront scheduling that pipelines waves based on their inter-task data dependencies. The wavefront schedule coordinates execution so that waves from different tasks and modalities overlap in time, filling pipeline bubbles caused by load imbalance.

title: GraphPipe: Improving Performance and Scalability of DNN Training with Graph Pipeline Parallelism
problem: Existing pipeline-parallel DNN training systems partition models into sequential stages, ignoring the actual DAG topology of modern neural networks, which causes missed model-parallelism opportunities and suboptimal device utilization.
method: GraphPipe introduces graph pipeline parallelism, which partitions a DNN's computation graph (DAG) rather than a linear sequence into pipeline stages. The system represents the DNN as a dataflow graph, identifies parallelizable subgraphs, and maps them to device groups that execute concurrently in a pipeline fashion. A graph-aware scheduling algorithm determines micro-batch execution order across non-linear pipeline stages to maximize throughput and minimize pipeline bubbles, coordinating across branches of the DAG.

title: Rewire: Advancing CGRA Mapping Through a Consolidated Routing Paradigm
problem: Existing CGRA compilers map dataflow graph nodes individually, neglecting inter-node dependencies; this leads to suboptimal placement that misses opportunities to exploit shared routing and structural locality.
method: Generates shareable routing information via propagation across multiple nodes, intersects routing sets to produce individual placement candidates, utilizes data dependencies as constraints to jointly place multiple nodes in one shot rather than individually.

title: Differentiable Net-Moving and Local Congestion Mitigation for Routability-Driven Global Placement
problem: Cell inflation for local congestion mitigation can over-inflate or move cells back into congested areas; global net bounding box minimization may include irrelevant congestion or miss actual bottlenecks; unbalanced placement density degrades pin accessibility.
method: Proposes momentum-based cell inflation tracking historical ratios for local congestion; constructs differentiable global congestion function from Poisson's equation with virtual standard cells on two-pin nets for accurate net movement guidance; adjusts placement density around power/ground rails per congestion patterns.
